title: RBAC: add permissions + least-privilege roles for data residency settings and violation summaries
author: Marcus Lin
body:
Summary: This PR introduces explicit RBAC permissions for (1) managing Hosted/Dedicated data residency settings (region pinning) and (2) viewing residency violation summaries in Console. It also adds least-privilege roles intended for Compliance/Security admins so they can self-serve residency configuration + evidence gathering without requiring full Org Admin privileges.

Motivation: The residency enforcement rollout (Hosted + Dedicated) adds new control surfaces in Console and new audit/telemetry views. Today, those endpoints are effectively gated by broad admin permissions. Enterprise customers have asked for separation-of-duties: Compliance can configure and monitor residency without having access to billing, API keys, or broader org management.

Scope / Changes: Add new permissions: - residency.settings.read: Read effective residency policy at org/project/workspace (pinned_region, allowed_regions, exception metadata) - residency.settings.write: Create/update residency policy (incl. enable/disable enforcement flags where applicable) - residency.violations.read: View aggregated violation summaries + recent events in Console (counts, last_seen, top endpoints/SDKs) - residency.exceptions.read: View exception status/expiry and approvals (where available in UI) - residency.exceptions.request: Create an exception request record (approval still enforced outside of RBAC scope; see exception workflow)

Role changes: - New role: Compliance Admin (org scope): residency.settings.read/write, residency.violations.read, residency.exceptions.read/request. No access to API keys, model configs, billing, or member management. - New role: Compliance Viewer (org scope): residency.settings.read, residency.violations.read, residency.exceptions.read. - Update existing role: Org Admin: unchanged (still has the new permissions implicitly via wildcard admin bundle) but now explicitly includes residency.* permissions for clarity.

Policy details / Notes: - Permissions are modeled as action strings consistent with existing bundle conventions ("<domain>.<resource>.<verb>"). - We intentionally split violations.read from settings.read so customers can grant evidence visibility without granting config write privileges. - Console endpoints for violation summaries should authorize against residency.violations.read (not settings.read) to avoid accidental privilege creep.

Implementation: - Add action definitions and documentation under policy schema docs. - Add role templates for Compliance Admin/Viewer with tests. - Add regression tests ensuring: (a) Compliance Admin can update residency policy but cannot rotate API keys; (b) Compliance Viewer can view violation summaries but cannot update policies; (c) Project-level admins do not gain org-level residency write unless explicitly granted.

Testing: - rego/unit: added tests for new roles and permission evaluation - bundle validation: schema + formatting checks - snapshot tests: updated expected role catalog output

Rollout / Backwards compatibility: - No behavior change for existing customers unless they assign the new roles. - Org Admin remains sufficient for all residency actions. - Console team can start gating new UI surfaces using these permissions immediately; feature flags remain handled in application layer.

Related: - Linear: ENG-2841 (policy model), ENG-2844 (audit events), DES-211 (Console UX) - Project: Hosted Data Residency Enforcement

Checklist: - [x] Added new actions to catalog - [x] Added role templates + docs - [x] Added unit tests and updated snapshots - [x] Coordinated permission names with Console team (Felix/Chloe)

Review conversation (highlights): Olga Petrov: "Can Compliance Viewer see raw request payloads or only summary counts? We need to avoid exposing prompt content via evidence views." Marcus Lin (author): "This bundle only gates actions; the Console endpoints are meant to show aggregate + metadata (region, timestamp, error_code). No prompt/completion content is included in violation summaries. I added a note in docs: violations views MUST NOT expose payload fields; payload visibility stays behind existing debug tooling permissions." Ethan Park: "Please ensure settings.write doesn’t implicitly grant project creation / config mutation. Some of our older roles are overly broad." Marcus Lin: "Confirmed. Settings.write only maps to residency settings endpoints; role template does not include project.* actions. Added regression test that Compliance Admin cannot create projects or update routing policies." Dylan Brooks: "Naming: prefer residency.policy.* over residency.settings.*? Console is using settings terminology." Marcus Lin: "Kept residency.settings.* to match Console and existing patterns (console: /settings/residency). Added an alias note in docs; if we want a policy namespace later, we can introduce it without breaking customers by adding additional actions." Felix Schneider: "Can we add residency.exceptions.read now even if exception workflow is still manual? We'll need to show exception status/expiry in the UI." Marcus Lin: "Added exceptions.read + exceptions.request. Approval still requires separate process, but UI can safely display exception objects gated by exceptions.read." 

Approvals: - Olga Petrov approved after doc note + tests - Ethan Park approved after regression test additions - Dylan Brooks approved with naming note

CI: - policy-lint: PASS - rego-tests: PASS (312 tests) - bundle-build: PASS

Merge: Squashed and merged to main.
